title: Isolating human intestinal crypts from biopsies for organoid generation
author: Ran RZ Zhou
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcqsivwe

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary materials by adjusting temperatures and warming plates.

substeps.instruction: Prechill PBS and 8mM EDTA in PBS on ice.
Pre-warm human organoid medium and 12-well/24-well plates in the tissue-culture incubator.

steps.title: Collect and wash biopsies
steps.instruction: Collect biopsy tissues (ranging from 6 to 20 mm3) and wash them to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Collect biopsies in PBS or culture media in 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Wash biopsies 3 times with 25 ml ice cold PBS each in 50 ml conical tubes, or until PBS looks clear.
Pool all tissues biopsied from the same site for downstream procedures.

steps.title: Incubate tissues in EDTA
steps.instruction: Incubate the pooled tissues to facilitate crypt release.

substeps.instruction: Incubate tissues from each biopsy in 25mL of 8 mM EDTA/PBS in a 50 ml conical tube for 30 min, rocking (not shaking) at 4°C.

steps.title: Prepare cell strainers
steps.instruction: Set up the filtration system on a 6-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Place one 100 um cell strainer on each well of a 6-well plate.
Pre-wet the cell strainer with 1mL culture media.

steps.title: Mechanically release crypts
steps.instruction: Use a customized pipette tip to vigorously release crypts from the biopsy tissue.

substeps.instruction: Transfer biopsies from EDTA/PBS into 1-2 ml ADF.
Customize a P1000 aerosol resistant tip by cutting it with a sterilized razor blade at a straight angle to be slightly smaller than the size of the largest biopsy.
Pipet up and down vigorously so the biopsy tissue goes in and out of the tip with some difficulty.

steps.title: Filter and collect crypts
steps.instruction: Separate the crypts from the remaining tissue and verify the yield.

substeps.instruction: Filter the tissue through the 100 um cell strainer to remove large pieces.
Collect the crypts into a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Verify that enough crypts were released using a microscope.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend crypts
steps.instruction: Pellet the crypts and resuspend them in growth media.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the crypts at 300-400 g at 4°C for 5 min in a tabletop swinging bucket centrifuge (avoid fixed angle microcentrifuges to ensure the pellet is at the bottom).
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the crypts in pre-warmed and CO2-equilibrated human organoid media (complete ADF) containing growth factors.

steps.title: Embed crypts in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Mix the crypts with Matrigel and plate them.

substeps.instruction: Mix crypts with thawed matrigel in a ratio of 1:2 (cells:matrigel), pipetting up and down while avoiding bubbles.
Plate the mixture onto a pre-warmed 12- or 24-well tissue culture plate at 100 ul/well or 50 ul/well, respectively.

steps.title: Incubate and add media
steps.instruction: Allow the Matrigel to set and provide nutrients for the organoids.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 45-60 min at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Add complete ADF into each well: 1 ml/well for 12-well plates or 0.5 ml/well for 24-well plates.

steps.title: Maintain and expand organoids
steps.instruction: Perform regular media changes and expansion.

substeps.instruction: Change media every other day with complete ADF.
Add ciprofloxacin (10 ug/ml) to the media to prevent bacterial contamination.
Split and expand organoids as needed, approximately once per week.
